items.stem:
Read the following extract on quaternary and quinary activities and outsourcing and answer the questions that follow.
"Quaternary activities involve the collection, production and dissemination of information. Personnel working in office buildings, schools and research labs belong to the quaternary sector. Quinary activities include the services of senior business executives, government officials, research scientists and financial and legal consultants."
(i) Which outsourcing involves highly skilled workers in fields such as research, legal services and e-learning? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'quinary activities' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Quinary activities are called gold collar professions. (1)
items.answer: (i) KPO (ii) Services that focus on the creation, re-arrangement and interpretation of new and existing ideas, performed by senior decision-makers. (iii) They involve highly paid senior decision-makers and specialised experts.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) KPO (ii) Services that focus on the creation, re-arrangement and interpretation of new and existing ideas, performed by senior decision-makers. (iii) They involve highly paid senior decision-makers and specialised experts.

Read the following extract on types of tertiary activities and answer the questions that follow.
"Services occur at many different levels, some to industry, some to people, and some to both. Periodic markets in rural areas are held where there are no regular markets. Tertiary activities include trade, transport, communication and services."
(i) Distance measured in the time taken to travel a route is called: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'wholesale trading' as it relates to this theme. (1)

items.answer: (i) time distance (ii) Trade through numerous intermediary merchants and supply houses, not directly with consumers. (iii) There is not enough demand to support regular daily markets.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) time distance (ii) Trade through numerous intermediary merchants and supply houses, not directly with consumers. (iii) There is not enough demand to support regular daily markets.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Periodic markets in rural areas are held where there are no regular markets. Most tertiary activities are performed by skilled labour, professionally trained experts and consultants. Services occur at many different levels, some to industry, some to people, and some to both. Tertiary activities include trade, transport, communication and services."
(i) Explain the term 'wholesale trading', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Tertiary activities require skilled labour. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Tertiary activities produce goods directly from nature." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) Trade through numerous intermediary merchants and supply houses, not directly with consumers. (ii) They involve the exchange of expertise and services rather than production of goods. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: They provide services; primary activities obtain goods directly from nature.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Trade through numerous intermediary merchants and supply houses, not directly with consumers. (ii) They involve the exchange of expertise and services rather than production of goods. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: They provide services; primary activities obtain goods directly from nature.
